memory_candidates.content: In BimodalLogic, where a new Lean declaration is FILED is a gate-cost decision, not only a design one, because the repository derives four independent generated surfaces from FormalSystem/ line counts: typst/generated/status.typ's formalsystem-line-count (commit-blocking via .githooks/pre-commit, which refuses any commit staging a .lean path while status.typ is stale), the per-file inventory row in that directory's own README.md generated block (checked by check-module-invariants.sh INV), the Live-lines-of-code totals block in the repository-root README.md, and the directory README's Last verified date under readme-lint.sh Check 4 (gated, ENFORCE_README_DATES=1). Adding one small computable measure beside DerivationTree.height in FormalSystem/ProofSystem/Derivation.lean therefore costs four reconciliation steps plus a full lake build --wfail of FormalSystem; filing the same measure in BimodalLib/Diagnostics/ costs none of them, because status.typ counts FormalSystem/, Tests/ and BimodalTools/ and not BimodalLib/. The reusable planning move: before siting a new declaration, ask which generated surfaces derive a quantity from the candidate directory, and check each one's commit-blocking/advisory posture, since a commit-blocking surface cannot be deferred to a reconciliation phase.
